units.en: His men seized the guests who had agreed about the hubs and beat every one of them to death.
units.literal: Several dozen men at his side seized those who had said the tree would make hubs and beat them all to death.

units.zh: 丁卯，帝至自南征。
units.en: On dingmao he returned from the south.
units.literal: On dingmao the Emperor returned from the southern campaign.

units.zh: 辛巳，天子命帝為相國，總百揆。
units.en: On xinsi the court named him Chancellor and head of government.
units.literal: On xinsi the Son of Heaven appointed the Emperor Chancellor and head of all government affairs.

units.zh: 以宣武、宣義、天平、護國、天雄、武順、佑國、河陽、義武、昭義、保義、武昭、武定、泰甯、平盧、匡國、武甯、忠義、荊南等二十一道為魏國。
units.en: Twenty-one circuits—from Xuanwu and Xuanyi to Jingnan—were carved into the state of Wei.
units.literal: Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, Huguo, Tianxiong, Wushun, Youguo, Heyang, Yiwu, Zhaoyi, Baoyi, Wuzhao, Wuding, Taining, Pinglu, Kuangguo, Wuning, Zhongyi, Jingnan, and twenty-one other circuits were made the state of Wei.

units.zh: 案《舊唐書》，尚有忠武、鎮國二道，此闕載。
units.en: The 《Old Tang History》 also lists Zhongwu and Zhenguo; this account omits them.
units.literal: Per the 《Old Tang History》, Zhongwu and Zhenguo two circuits are also included; they are omitted here.

units.zh: 進封帝為魏王，入朝不趨，劍履上殿，贊拜不名，兼備九錫之命。
units.en: He was made Prince of Wei with the full honors of the Nine Bestowals—no need to hurry at court, sword and shoes in the throne room, his name unspoken in praise.
units.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, granted not to hasten at court audience, to enter with sword and shoes, not to be named when praised, and invested with the full Nine Bestowals.

units.zh: 癸未，唐中書門下奏：「中書印已送相國，中書公事權用中書省印。」
units.en: On guiwei the Secretariat reported, "Its seal had gone to the Chancellor, and routine business would use the office seal instead."
units.literal: On guiwei the Tang Secretariat memorialized, "The Secretariat seal has been sent to the Chancellor; Secretariat business shall provisionally use the Secretariat Office seal."

units.zh: 甲申，中書門下奏：「天下州縣名與相國魏王家諱同者，請易之。」
units.en: On jiashen they asked, "Every place whose name matched a Wei princely taboo should be renamed."
units.literal: On jiashen the Secretariat memorialized, "Wherever prefecture and county names match the taboo names of the Chancellor Prince of Wei's house, we ask that they be changed."

units.zh: 十二月乙酉朔，帝讓相國、魏王、九錫之命。
units.en: On the twelfth month's new moon he declined the Chancellorship, the princedom, and the Nine Bestowals.
units.literal: On the yiyou new moon in the twelfth month the Emperor declined the appointments as Chancellor, Prince of Wei, and the Nine Bestowals.

units.zh: 丙戌，京百司各差官齎本司須知孔目並印赴魏國送納。
units.en: On bingxu every capital agency sent clerks with its ledgers and seals to Wei.
units.literal: On bingxu each office of the capital dispatched officials bearing that office's essential registers and seals to the state of Wei for delivery.

units.zh: 甲午，天子以帝堅讓九錫之命。
units.en: On jiawu, since he still refused the Nine Bestowals,
units.literal: On jiawu the Son of Heaven, because the Emperor firmly declined the Nine Bestowals,

units.zh: 乃命宰相柳燦來使，且述揖讓之意焉。
units.en: the court sent Chancellor Liu Can to argue the matter and speak of abdication.
units.literal: then ordered Chancellor Liu Can to come as envoy and also set forth the meaning of yielding the throne.

units.zh: 丁酉，帝又讓九錫之命，詔略曰：「但以鴻名難掩，懿實須彰，宜且徇于奏陳，未便行於典冊。」
units.en: On dingyou he refused again; the edict read in part, "Your merit cannot be hidden—oblige us for now, but hold off the formal investiture."
units.literal: On dingyou the Emperor again declined the Nine Bestowals; the edict in summary said, "But the great name is hard to conceal and true merit must be displayed—for now yield to the memorials; do not yet proceed to the canonical registers."

units.zh: 又改諸道兵馬元帥為天下兵馬元帥。
units.en: He was retitled commander-in-chief of all forces under heaven.
units.literal: He also changed Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits to Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven.

units.zh: 是時，帝以唐朝百官服飾多闕，乃製造逐色衣服，請朝廷等第賜之。
units.en: Court dress was in tatters; he had robes made in every grade and asked the throne to distribute them by rank.
units.literal: At this time, because Tang court officials' robes and regalia were largely lacking, the Emperor manufactured garments of every color and asked the court to bestow them by rank.

units.zh: 其所給俸錢，仍請自來年正月全支。
units.en: He also asked that full salaries resume from the first month of the new year.
units.literal: As for the salary money granted them, he still asked that full payment begin from the first month of the coming year.

units.zh: 三年正月，幽、滄稱兵，將寇于魏。
units.en: In the third year's first month the Yan and Cang armies marched against Wei.
units.literal: In the first month of the third year You and Cang raised troops and were about to invade Wei.

units.zh: 魏人來乞師，且以牙軍驕悍，謀欲誅之，遣親吏臧延范密告於帝，帝陰許之。
units.en: Wei sought aid and plotted to slaughter its unruly guard corps; Zang Yanfan secretly asked the Emperor, who quietly agreed.
units.literal: The people of Wei came to beg for troops, and because the guard corps was arrogant and fierce they plotted to execute them, sending a close clerk Zang Yanfan to inform the Emperor in secret; the Emperor secretly assented.

units.zh: 乙丑，北征。
units.en: On yichou he marched north.
units.literal: On yichou he campaigned north.

units.zh: 先是，帝之愛女適羅氏，是月卒於鄴城，因以兵仗數千事實於橐中，遣客將馬嗣勳領長直軍千人，雜以工匠、丁夫，肩其橐而入于魏，聲言為帝女設祭，魏人信而不疑。
units.en: His favorite daughter, wed to the Luo house, had died at Yecheng that month. He packed thousands of weapons in funeral chests and sent Ma Sixun with a thousand guards, artisans, and porters to carry them into Wei under cover of mourning rites—and no one suspected.
units.literal: Earlier the Emperor's beloved daughter had married into the Luo clan; that month she died at Yecheng. Thereupon several thousand weapons and gear were packed in coffers, and Guest General Ma Sixun was sent to lead a thousand men of the permanent guard, mixed with artisans and laborers, to shoulder the coffers into Wei, claiming they were for sacrifices for the Emperor's daughter; the people of Wei believed it and suspected nothing.

units.zh: 庚午夜，嗣勳率其眾與羅紹威親軍數百人同攻牙軍，遲明盡殺之，死者七千餘人，泊於嬰孺，亦無留者。
units.en: At midnight on gengwu Sixun and Shaowei's guard fell on the guard corps; by dawn seven thousand were dead, infants included, without a survivor.
units.literal: At midnight on gengwu Sixun led his men and several hundred of Luo Shaowei's personal guard to attack the guard corps together; by dawn they had killed them all—more than seven thousand dead, down to infants in arms, none left alive.

units.zh: 是日，帝次於內黃，聞之，馳騎至魏。
units.en: That day he was at Neihuang; hearing the news, he galloped to Wei.
units.literal: That day the Emperor was halted at Neihuang; hearing of it, he galloped to Wei.

units.zh: 時魏之大軍方與帝軍同伐滄州，聞牙軍之死，即時奔還。
units.en: Wei's main force, campaigning at Cangzhou beside him, turned back the moment the guard corps was wiped out.
units.literal: At this time Wei's main army was campaigning against Cangzhou together with the Emperor's army; hearing of the guard corps' destruction, they immediately fled back.

units.zh: 帝之軍追及曆亭，殺賊幾千，餘眾乃擁大將史仁遇保于高唐，帝遣兵圍之。
units.en: His troops overtook them at Liting, killed thousands, and penned the rest under Shi Renyu at Gaotang, which he then besieged.
units.literal: The Emperor's army caught them at Liting, killed several thousand bandits, and the remainder then rallied around General Shi Renyu and held Gaotang; the Emperor sent troops to besiege them.

units.zh: 是月，天子詔河南尹張全義部署修制相國魏王法物。
units.en: That month the court ordered Zhang Quanyi to prepare the Prince of Wei's ceremonial regalia.
units.literal: That month the Son of Heaven ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to arrange the manufacture of regalia for the Chancellor Prince of Wei.

units.zh: 三月甲寅，天子命帝總判鹽鐵、度支、戶部等三司事，帝再上章切讓之，乃止。
units.en: On jiayin he was ordered to head the salt, revenue, and treasury offices; he declined again by memorial and the appointment lapsed.
units.literal: On jiayin in the third month the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to oversee the Salt, Revenue, and Treasury commissions; the Emperor again memorialized urgently declining, and it stopped.

units.zh: 四月癸未，攻下高唐，軍民無少長皆殺之，生擒逆首史仁遇以獻，帝命支解之。
units.en: On guiwei Gaotang fell; every soul inside was killed; Shi Renyu was taken alive and dismembered on the Emperor's order.
units.literal: On guiwei in the fourth month Gaotang was taken; soldiers and civilians, none young or old, were all killed; the rebel leader Shi Renyu was captured alive and presented; the Emperor ordered him dismembered.

units.zh: 未幾，又攻下澶、博、貝、衛等州，皆為魏軍殘黨所據故也。
units.en: Soon Chan, Bo, Bei, and Wei fell as well—holdouts of the Wei mutineers.
units.literal: Before long they also took Chan, Bo, Bei, and Wei prefectures—all because remnant bands of the Wei army still held them.

units.zh: 是時晉人圍邢州，刺史牛存節堅壁固守，帝遣符道昭帥師救之，晉人乃遁去。
units.en: Jin besieged Xingzhou while Niu Cunjie held firm; Fu Daozhao relieved the city and Jin withdrew.
units.literal: At this time the Jin people besieged Xing Prefecture; Prefect Niu Cunjie held the walls firmly; the Emperor sent Fu Daozhao to lead troops to rescue them, and the Jin people then fled away.

units.zh: 五月，帝略地於洺州，既而復入于魏。
units.en: In the fifth month he raided Mingzhou and returned to Wei.
units.literal: In the fifth month the Emperor raided the lands of Ming Prefecture, then again entered Wei.

units.zh: 七月己未，自魏班師。
units.en: On jiwei in the seventh month he withdrew from Wei.
units.literal: On jiwei in the seventh month he withdrew his army from Wei.

units.zh: 是日，收復相州，自是魏境悉平。
units.en: That same day Xiangzhou was recovered and Wei's territory was fully pacified.
units.literal: That day Xiang Prefecture was recovered; from then on the Wei territory was entirely pacified.

units.zh: 壬申，帝歸自魏。
units.en: On renshen he returned from Wei.
units.literal: On renshen the Emperor returned from Wei.

units.zh: 八月甲辰，以滄州未平，復命北征。
units.en: On jiachen in the eighth month, Cangzhou still holding out, he marched north again.
units.literal: On jiachen in the eighth month, because Cangzhou was not yet pacified, he was again ordered to campaign north.

units.zh: 九月丁卯，營于長蘆。
units.en: On dingmao in the ninth month he camped at Changlu.
units.literal: On dingmao in the ninth month he encamped at Changlu.

units.zh: 一夕，帝夢白龍附於兩肩，左右瞻顧可畏，怳然驚寤。
units.en: One night he dreamed a white dragon coiled on both shoulders—terrifying when he glanced aside—and woke with a start.
units.literal: One night the Emperor dreamed a white dragon clung to both his shoulders; looking left and right it was fearsome to behold, and he started awake in a daze.

units.zh: 十月辛巳，邠州楊崇本以鳳翔、邠、寧、涇、鄜、秦、隴之眾合五六萬來寇，屯于美原，列十五寨，其勢甚盛。
units.en: On xinsi Yang Chongben of Binzhou led fifty or sixty thousand from Fengxiang, Bin, Ning, and the western circuits to Meiyuan in fifteen camps—a formidable host.
units.literal: On xinsi in the tenth month Yang Chongben of Bin Prefecture, with the hosts of Fengxiang, Bin, Ning, Jing, Fu, Qin, and Long—fifty or sixty thousand in all—came to invade, encamped at Meiyuan, and set fifteen camps; their momentum was very strong.

units.zh: 帝命同州節度使劉知俊、都將康懷英帥師禦之。
units.en: He sent Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou and Kang Huaiying to meet them.
units.literal: The Emperor ordered Tong Prefecture Military Governor Liu Zhijun and Chief Commander Kang Huaiying to lead troops to resist them.

units.zh: 知俊等大破邠寇，殺二萬餘眾，奪馬三千餘匹，擒其列校百餘人，楊崇本、胡章僅以身免。
units.en: Zhijun routed them—twenty thousand dead, three thousand horses taken, a hundred officers captured; Yang Chongben and Hu Zhang fled with their lives.
units.literal: Zhijun and the others greatly defeated the Bin invaders, killing more than twenty thousand, seizing more than three thousand horses, capturing more than a hundred of their officers, and Yang Chongben and Hu Zhang barely escaped with their lives.

units.zh: 十一月庚戌，懷英乘勝進軍，遂收鄜州。
units.en: On gengxu Huaiying pressed on and took Fuzhou.
units.literal: On gengxu in the eleventh month Huaiying pressed the victory and advanced, then recovered Fu Prefecture.

units.zh: 十二月乙丑，帝以文武常參官每月一、五、九日赴朝，奏請備廊餐，詔從之。
units.en: On yichou in the twelfth month he asked that officials attending court on the 1st, 5th, and 9th be fed in the corridor; the court agreed.
units.literal: On yichou in the twelfth month, because civil and military regular officials attended court on the first, fifth, and ninth of each month, the Emperor memorialized asking that corridor meals be provided; the edict assented.

units.zh: 遂自長蘆班師。
units.en: He then withdrew from Changlu.
units.literal: He then withdrew his army from Changlu.

units.zh: 案：以上疑有闕文。
units.en: Editorial note: text appears to be missing above this point.
units.literal: Note: the text above is suspected to be missing.

units.zh: 據《舊唐書·哀帝紀》：戊辰，李克用與幽州之眾同攻潞州，全忠守將丁會以澤、潞降太原，克用以其子嗣昭為留後。
units.en: The 《Old Tang History · Annals of Emperor Ai》 records that on wuchen Li Keyong and the Youzhou army besieged Luzhou; Ding Hui, Quanzhong's garrison commander, surrendered Ze and Lu to Taiyuan, and Keyong made his son Sizhao governor.
units.literal: Per the 《Old Tang History · Basic Annals of Emperor Ai》: On wuchen Li Keyong with the Youzhou host jointly attacked Luzhou; Quanzhong's defending general Ding Hui surrendered Ze and Lu to Taiyuan, and Keyong installed his son Sizhao as acting governor.

units.zh: 甲戌，全忠燒長蘆營旋軍，聞潞州陷故也。
units.en: On jiaxu Quanzhong burned the camp at Changlu and marched back on news that Luzhou had fallen.
units.literal: On jiaxu Quanzhong burned the Changlu camp and turned his army back, because he had heard Luzhou had fallen.

units.zh: 以寨內糗糧山積，帝命焚之。
units.en: The camp held grain in mountain heaps; the Emperor ordered it all burned.
units.literal: Because provisions in the camp were heaped like mountains, the Emperor ordered them burned.

units.zh: 滄帥劉守文以城中絕食，因致書於帝，乞留餘糧以救饑民，帝為留十餘囷以與之。
units.en: Liu Shouwen of Cangzhou, the city starving, wrote begging spare grain for the people; the Emperor left a dozen-odd granaries for them.
units.literal: Cangzhou Military Governor Liu Shouwen, because the city was entirely without food, thereupon sent a letter to the Emperor begging that the remaining grain be left to save the starving people; the Emperor left more than ten granaries' worth and gave them to him.

units.zh: 《容齋續筆》：滄州還師，悉焚諸營資糧，在舟中者鑿而沉之。
units.en: The 《Rongzhai Continued Notes》 says that on the withdrawal from Cangzhou every store was burned and boatloads were scuttled.
units.literal: The 《Rongzhai Continued Notes》 says: On the return from Cangzhou he burned all camp stores; what was aboard boats was bored through and sunk.

units.zh: 守文遺全忠書曰：「城中數萬口，不食數月矣，與其焚之為煙，沉之為泥，願乞其所餘以救之。」
units.en: Shouwen wrote Quanzhong: "Tens of thousands in the city have starved for months—better you spare what is left than burn it to smoke or sink it in the river."
units.literal: Shouwen wrote to Quanzhong, "Tens of thousands in the city have gone without food for months; rather than burn it to smoke or sink it to mud, I beg what remains to save them."

units.zh: 全忠為之留數囷，滄人賴以濟。
units.en: Quanzhong spared several granaries, and Cangzhou lived through the famine on them.
units.literal: Quanzhong left several granaries for them, and the people of Cang relied on it to survive.
